title: I work nights at a twenty-four hour laundromat. Dryer nine keeps running without anyone putting money in it.
story:
The first time it happened, it was just after two in the morning. The laundromat was empty, the street was dark, and dryer nine started tumbling all by itself.

I figured it was a stuck coin. I opened the door to check. Inside was a single gray hoodie, warm and turning slowly.

I own a gray hoodie just like it. I was wearing it.

I told myself a lot of people have gray hoodies. I folded it, put it in the lost and found, and went back to my phone.

The next night, dryer nine started again. This time it was jeans with a torn left knee, and a single blue sock. I looked down at my own torn knee. I could feel my left foot, bare inside my shoe. I had only put on one sock that morning and didn't notice.

Every night after that, it was something I was wearing. A scarf. A watch with a cracked face. My work badge, with my name on it, still warm.

Tonight the dryer started at two again. I didn't open it. I just watched through the round glass.

It's not clothes this time.

It's turning slowly, and it has my face.
premise: laundromat dryer runs on its own, each night drying an item the narrator is wearing; finally the narrator
